OSes for phones are small compared to a console, and a console's OS is not downloaded in massive chunks but hot-patch updates in most circumstances (though there have been a few XBox patches that ranged in the 6-8g range in the last 15 years or so). Operating systems are also not patched whole-part but piece-meal (updating portions of the operating system as needed, not complete updates that replace the whole OS).

The fact that you don't pay for tv is also irrelevant. You are consuming media. You are apparently in a contract that provides you with X amount of bandwidth and you are using X+Y amount of bandwidth. That's what happens when you consume more than your contracted allowance. You don't get to have your cake (avoid commercial television) and eat it too (stream whatever you want commercial free and not pay for it).

I just finished reading The Savage Detectives by Roberto Bolano.

This book is both brilliant and frustrating. Though it's not the easiest book to sum up in a short paragraph, The Savage Detectives is about a group of "visceral realists", a Mexican poetry movement that seems to do everything but write poetry. The two "main" characters, Ulises Lima and Arturo Belano, are loosely based on Bolano himself, two of his alter egos, if you will. I put "main" in quotes, because this book is mostly told in first person narrative by pretty much everyone in the movement except for Lima and Belano. This, coupled with the constant Latin poetry references and in-jokes make it not the easiest thing to read at first. My advice - let it go. You don't have to know who any of these people are to appreciate the novel. I thought of them as universal archetypes who can stand in for individuals we all know in any artistic club or movement.

Red Mars by Kim Stanley Robinson

This is not my first time reading it, but there is so much in there that multiple trips are rewarding. It's a hard Sci-fi trilogy about the first 100 colonists on Mars, the attempts by humans to terraform the red planet, and the ethics of if they even should attempt it. It's a great read if you love mars, space, or even colonization theory. It's not for readers looking for constant action and high romance though it has it's moments.
